messages.body_plain:
Hi!
I was delighted to find out that RKWard 0.8.0 is here!
Since it might take time so that the conservative linux distributions use
qt6, could it be possible to add the official release to the
appimage.github.io directory?
So that it can be installed from AppImage Pool (a flatpack app), it
would require that the GitHub repository hosts AppImages on its Releases
page.

Regards
Alfonso

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

On Sun, 4 Aug 2024 21:29:29 -0600
DES Alfonso Cano Robles <alfonsociologo at gmail.com> wrote:
> I was delighted to find out that RKWard 0.8.0 is here!
> Since it might take time so that the conservative linux distributions
> use qt6, could it be possible to add the official release to the
> appimage.github.io directory?
> So that it can be installed from AppImage Pool (a flatpack app), it
> would require that the GitHub repository hosts AppImages on its
> Releases page.

in principle, this sounds good, and you're quite welcome to submit our
AppImage for publication in that pool (or wherever else - it's free
software, after all)!

The more difficult step is to keep the information up to date, in the
long term. Making releases is a heavily bureaucratic exercise, already,
and such updates are simply something that we _will_ forget. You are
right in pointing out that this particular process could be automated,
if our AppImages were hosted on github. Alas, that's not the case (and
I'm not sure that can easily be done).

Regards
Thomas

Hi,
I hope you are well!
I've been trying out to install RKWard on two  arm computers.

With the first one, I Initially tried with the mac arm stable from:
https://download.kde.org/stable/rkward/0.8.0/rkward-0.8.0-arm64.dmg
With no success, it comes at the end of the installation process, it
started R 4.4.1 correctly but closed unexpectedly just when it tried to
show the html welcome screen.

Then I tried the nightly build,
- rkward-master-1346-macos-clang-arm64.dmg
but I've had the same issue.

Here I attached the rkward.frontend file along with the Translate Report,
It is a M1 chip.
As far as I can tell it is related with:

> Path override failed for key base::DIR_APP_DICTIONARIES and path
> '/Applications/rkward.app/Contents/MacOS/qtwebengine_dictionaries'

I hope this helps to fix the problem.

About the second computer I'll send the info in a separate email,

I thank you for  everything you have done and your help!
Alfonso
-- 
Dr. Alfonso Cano Robles

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

On Fri, 16 Aug 2024 10:11:40 -0600
DES Alfonso Cano Robles <alfonsociologo at gmail.com> wrote:
> I've been trying out to install RKWard on two  arm computers.

thanks. Both crash at the same point:

Crashed Thread:        33  Chrome_InProcRendererThread

Exception Type:        EXC_BREAKPOINT (SIGTRAP)
Exception Codes:       0x0000000000000001, 0x00000001863acf08

Termination Reason:    Namespace SIGNAL, Code 5 Trace/BPT trap: 5
Terminating Process:   exc handler [1426]

where the backtrace of Thread 33 is:

Thread 33 Crashed:: Chrome_InProcRendererThread
0 libsystem_pthread.dylib  0x1863acf08 pthread_jit_write_protect_np
1 QtWebEngineCore 0x114d3e7ec 0x10f2dc000 + 94775276

So, yes, this is a problem with QWebEngine, again. More specifically it
seems to be related to the JIT-compiler, which makes me think of a
permissions/entitlements problem, immediately.

I'll try something, but this may take some time.

Merely out of curiosity: If, instead, you install the x86 version of
RKWard on that machine, do you see anything different? (Note that you
will not be able to start the R backend, then, but you should be able
to skip over that with "Cancel". The interesting part, here, is whether
the welcome screen gets rendered.)

Regards
Thomas
